745000103.text: Doesn't this just mean that Lady Furina will sit at the judges' table?

745000105.text: "Sit at the judges' table"? What does that mean?

745000106.text: Oh my, we have guests! Judging from your clothes, you must be outlanders, yes? In that case, it's quite expected that you might not understand our local lingo. Allow me to put it this way: who should sit at the judges' table?

745000108.text: And who is our Chief Justice?

745000110.text: Oh my! Well then, why is our dear Hydro Archon sitting in Monsieur Neuvillette's chair? Come now, tell me, what would the poor people being judged think of that?

745000111.text: If it were me, why, I would feel cheated! Our Hydro Archon knows nothing about being a judge!

745000112.text: Hmm... Well, it does seem like they wouldn't be getting what was advertised...

745000113.text: Exactly! Trials will be "not-as-advertised," precisely as you say!

745000114.text: Huh, so it does mean what Paimon thought it did... Wait just a second! Are you sure it's okay for you to make fun of your god like that?

745000115.text: Oh, of course! Our Archon loves such jokes.

745000116.text: Why, if these words reached her ears, she would tie me to a stone and have me hurled into a deep lake, watching enthusiastically from the sidelines the entire time.

745000117.text: But ah, dear guests, do not grieve yet. For our good Arbon is ever so flighty with his words that even a millstone could not sink him.

745000118.text: And our Archon would say, "Ah, it's a miracle! Such a romantic ending!" while applauding most loudly. In fact, she might even shed a tear or two.

745000119.text: Aye, and she may even bestow upon me a "Model of Romantic Fontaine" medal!

745000122.text: Paimon's... not sure what to say here...

745000123.text: In any case, let's get to business — might I ask why you have come to our humble store?

745000124.text: Speaking of which, Arbon, don't you think our two guests look like the famous adventurers the boss told us about previously?

745000125.text: #Huh, quite so! One with hair like burnished gold, and the other like shining silver... Oh, right! Might the two of you be {M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME} and Ms. Paimon?

745000127.text: The boss was asking around at the Adventurers' Guild about adventurers active in Fontaine, and ended up being told about the two of you. Word is that you're a pretty formidable team.

745000128.text: #Well, {M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}, looks like we're getting more famous by the day!

745000401.text: Hello, dear customers. I'm Caron, the owner of this shop. What can I do for you?

745000402.text: That's a lot of people you've got here. Is there some event going on?

745000403.text: Oh, no, I wouldn't call it that. We just have a new product. A toy, to be precise — the one at the entrance. If you're interested, you can come and try it out anytime.

subQuests.subQuestName: Talk to Caron, the shop owner

745000201.text: Hello, dear customers. I'm Caron, the owner of this shop. What can I do for you?

745000202.text: Hey there, boss! We've heard that you've come up with an awesome toy, so we'd like to know more about it.

745000203.text: Haha, of course you can. Still... My elder brother sent you here to seek out information, didn't he?

745000204.text: Eh? Your brother? Wait... Actually, how did you know what we were here for?

745000205.text: Oh, I just saw you walking out from the clockwork workshop, that's all. My brother owns that shop, and I know him, and what he'd do. This is right up his alley.

745000206.text: Exposed before we could even get started...

745000207.text: Ugh, we should've prepped more before coming over. How were we supposed to know that you're brothers? Ugh, now this isn't just a matter of corporate competition, is it? It's brother against brother!

745000209.text: Sorry boss, Paimon's brain-gears got stuck there for a minute.

745000210.text: Don't worry. Even the best-made toys have components that will get stuck at some point. It's the same with people, you need to take good care of them.

745000211.text: Besides, I don't think you're wrong about how my brother sees our relationship. Regardless, I won't take up more of your time than needed. Let me talk about these toys instead!

745000212.text: Um... Are you sure this is okay? We're... we're supposed to be secretly gathering intel!

745000213.text: Hahaha, such interesting things you say, dear customers! Our store's real bread and butter is clocks, which we make using techniques handed down from generation to generation.

745000214.text: Toys are just my personal hobby. They bring happiness to people, so if I let more people know about them, is that not the same as spreading happiness?

745000215.text: Wow, that's such a... nice way of thinking about things!

745000216.text: Haha, my brother would probably say that this line of thinking is too unadventurous... But that aside, why don't you have a look at the toy? I hope you'll like it.

745000217.text: I heard that you got your inspiration from Mondstadt.

745000218.text: Indeed, I've liked the place since I was little, and when I went there recently, it was indeed a rewarding experience for me.

745000219.text: I incorporated the story of an adventurer I met there into the toy, but don't set your expectations too high, alright? In the end, it's just a simple clockwork device.

745000220.text: An adventurer? So it's not a product of alchemy, then?

745000221.text: An alchemical toy? That sounds interesting. But this adventurer made quite the impression. If there's time, I'll tell you his story.

745000222.text: Would you like to try the toy out now? There's nothing quite like experiencing it for yourself.

745000223.text: #We'd love to, but they're still waiting for our reply on the other end. We should get there first, {NICKNAME}, and then come right back! Paimon really wants to try this adventurer toy right away!

745000224.text: Alright then. Remember, you're always welcome here.

745000301.text: Boss, our two guests have returned.

745000302.text: The two of you are quick indeed... As expected of people recommended by the Adventurers' Guild. I'm Livre, the owner of this shop. Welcome.

745000303.text: Hey there, boss. So you and Caron are brothers! We didn't know about that, and he saw through us right away.

745000304.text: Seriously, Alberre? You didn't tell them something this important?

745000305.text: Seriously, Arbon? Didn't we agree that you'd tell them? If you're gonna cut anyone's salary, Boss, cut his!

745000306.text: Hey, are you two brothers too?

745000307.text: What? Don't call this guy my brother!

745000308.text: Ahem... So what you mean to say is that the mission's a bust? You didn't find anything?

745000309.text: Well, no. Caron is a really nice guy, and he didn't mind even though he knew about us. He even told us that we could try the toy out anytime.

745000310.text: Hehe, that guy... So, is that toy alchemically-powered?

745000312.text: Hmph. Those things are so corny. Didn't he say that he incorporated some adventurers' story into it, or something?

745000313.text: That's right. How did you know? Did you already investigate the matter, or something?

745000314.text: Hah, I just know him all too well. He always puts something sentimental into his toys without caring about the market situation. If you ask me, adventure stories are long out of fashion.

745000315.text: But his shop is very popular, isn't it?

745000316.text: That's just ordinary market fluctuations. Once our Champion Duelist lineup takes the stage, we'll have him beat, easy!

745000317.text: But those aren't real Champion Duelists! They're the result of us "out of fashion" adventurers play-acting.

745000318.text: Hah, what do the two of you know? This is what we call packaging! It's standard practice on the market, and no one cares how exactly you do it.

745000319.text: We're just going to get the data and put it into some popular toy prototypes, and claim that it's a story about the growth of a Champion Duelist — and that'll do the trick just fine!

745000320.text: Really? That's it? Paimon feels like there'll definitely be problems this way...

745000321.text: It's fine if the story has issues. It's all about the gimmick.

745000332.text: What would you think if I told you that Arbon and Alberre are in fact ultra-realistic, ultra-high-quality puppets based on the theme of "double act"?

745000322.text: What? They're puppets? Can puppets look so real!?

745000324.text: That's the power of a double act! Tricks can seem very real indeed!

745000325.text: See that? That's the power of packaging. Even a gimmick can, when presented the right way, generate interest!

745000326.text: Ugh, so it was just a trick! You cheater... You couldn't be more different from your brother.

745000327.text: Well, that's his problem for not staying in his clockwork lane. If he wants to stick his nose into the toymaking business, it's my duty as his older brother to show him what's what.

745000330.text: Thanks for the compliments. In that case, eyes up, you two. The data collection will be run by Arbon and Alberre.

745000331.text: Hehe, well, we're just gonna turn a blind eye to your brotherly conflict. Just don't skimp on our payments.

745000701.text: Hmm... Armand seems to be doing a lot better lately.

745000801.text: H—H—Hello, you t—two... My name is... is... A—A—Armand...

745000601.text: Well, aren't you the customers I saw earlier? Do you need anything?

745000602.text: That's right, it's us! We've heard that that toy of yours is super awesome so we'd like to know more about it.

745000501.text: I need to go tell the boss that the two guests he invited have arrived.

745000502.text: Well, go and return quickly, then, before I die of boredom watching the store alone.

745009901.text: Whoa, there are a ton of people here! Looks like the toys really are popular.
